usageNotes: Use this to create a new SDN VNet object within an existing SDN zone. The caller must hold SDN.Allocate on the target zone (/sdn/zones/{zone}). After creation, the new VNet does not take effect on cluster nodes until you apply the pending SDN configuration via PUT /cluster/sdn; VMs will not see the network until that apply step completes.

examples.summary: Create a VXLAN-backed VNet named 'prodnet' in the 'evpnzone' zone with a VXLAN VNI of 10001

tips: The 'vnet' identifier must be 2–8 alphanumeric characters, start with a letter, and end with a letter or digit — plan names carefully since renaming requires delete and recreate.
Set 'vlanaware' to true only if VMs on this VNet need to trunk multiple VLANs across the bridge (e.g., for nested virtualisation or router-on-a-stick setups).
Enable 'isolate-ports' to prevent VM-to-VM traffic on the same bridge without going through a router, useful for zero-trust or tenant-isolation scenarios.
Changes are staged — always follow up with PUT /cluster/sdn to push the pending configuration to all nodes.
The lock-token parameter is only needed if you are coordinating concurrent SDN writes and have obtained a lock; most single-operator workflows can omit it.
